name: Monk Warrior-Monk
body:
Warrior-monks focus on martial combat and entering a state of martial focus and power. In certain cultures, these monks are called sohei. Some think of them as a combination of the Western paladin and a monk, but this is not a true comparison. Sohei are typically associated with spiritualist religions, are vehement in the protection of their religion, and willing to go to war, they are not like holy questing knights.

Spiritual Frenzy (Ex)

At 1st level, a warrior-monk can enter a religiously-inspired frenzy of combat. This frenzy lasts for 1 minute and can be used a number of times per day equal to their Wisdom modifier. While in this frenzy, the warrior-monk gains a +4 morale bonus to Strength and Dexterity and a +2 morale bonus to Will saves. Additionally, they gain use of their flurry of blows and fast movement abilities. Those two abilities are not usable outside of their spiritual frenzy. Entering this frenzy is a free action usable on their turn.

While in this frenzy, the warrior-monk is unable to use any Charisma-, Wisdom-, or Intelligence-based skills, cast spells, or use any ability or feat that requires concentration, like Combat Expertise.

The warrior-monk can end their spiritual frenzy at any time as a free action. At the end of this frenzy, the warrior-monk is fatigued for the number of rounds spent in the spiritual frenzy.

This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 1st level and modifies flurry of blows and fast movement.

Focused Weapon (Ex)

At 1st level, a warrior-monk is trained in the use of a weapon of their religious order.

They choose one melee weapon, which cannot be changed later. They gain Weapon Focus for this weapon and treat it as a monk weapon. The weapon’s damage is treated as the greater of the weapon’s normal damage or their unarmed damage. Any abilities or feats delivered through a monk’s unarmed strike can be delivered through the focused weapon. The traditional weapon for these warrior-monks is the naginata.

This ability replaces stunning fist.

Diehard (Ex)

At 2nd level, a warrior-monk hones their body and mind to be resilient in combat. They gain Diehard as a bonus feat. If they are using spiritual frenzy, they are not staggered while below 0 hp.

This ability replaces evasion.

Mettle (Ex)

At 9th level, a warrior-monk becomes very resilient in their body and mind. Anytime they succeed on a spell effect that would impose a partial effect on a Fortitude or Will save, they instead are unaffected.

This ability replaces improved evasion.

Greater Spiritual Frenzy (Ex)

At 12th level, a warrior-monk increases the bonuses to Strength and Dexterity gained from spiritual frenzy to +6 and the bonus to Will saves increases to +3.

This ability replaces abundant step.

Tireless Spiritual Frenzy (Ex)

At 17th level, a warrior-monk is no longer fatigued when ending their spiritual frenzy.

This ability replaces timeless body.

Master Spiritual Frenzy (Ex)

At 20th level, a warrior-monk’s frenzy is beyond compare. The bonuses to Strength and Dexterity from their spiritual frenzy increase to +8, and their bonus to Will saves increases to +4.

This ability replaces perfect self.
